merger_description:
Accenture Inc., a wholly-owned subsidiary of Accenture plc (together with its direct and indirect subsidiaries, **Accenture**) proposes to acquire 100% of the shares in a global creator and social media tech-enabled service business with proprietary platforms carved out from the Whalar Group (**Whalar Agency**) (the **Acquisition**).

Accenture is a global professional services company headquartered in Dublin, Ireland. It provides a broad range of services across strategy, consulting, digital, technology, and operations designed to assist public and private clients by bringing client-specific industry solutions and services to accelerate reinvention and value creation.

Accenture (through ‘Accenture Song’ (**Song**), a tech-powered creative group), creates customer-led growth focusing on end-to-end customer agendas and bringing together customer growth strategy, marketing, sales, service, commerce, design, digital products, data and AI.

Whalar Agency comprises the Whalar Group’s creator and influencer marketing services agency that designs, executes and measures end-to-end influencer marketing campaigns for enterprise brands, supported by proprietary AI-enabled technology.

determination_table_content.details:
Accenture Inc., a wholly-owned subsidiary of Accenture plc (together
with its direct and indirect subsidiaries, Accenture), applied for a
notification waiver in respect of its proposed acquisition of 100% of
the shares in Whalar Agency, as described in the transaction
documents provided as part of the application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, Accenture, is a global professional services company
headquartered in Dublin, Ireland. It provides a broad range of
services across strategy, consulting, digital, technology, and
operations designed to assist public and private clients by bringing
client-specific industry solutions and services to accelerate
reinvention and value creation.
Accenture, through ‘Accenture Song’ (a tech-powered creative
group), creates customer-led growth focusing on end-to-end
customer agendas and bringing together customer growth strategy,
marketing, sales, service, commerce, design, digital products, data
and AI.
The target, Whalar Agency, is a global creator and social media tech-
enabled service business with proprietary platforms carved out from
the Whalar Group.
Whalar Agency comprises the Whalar Group’s creator and influencer
marketing services agency that designs, executes and measures
end-to-end influencer marketing campaigns for enterprise brands,
supported by proprietary AI-enabled technology.
The parties both supply marketing and communications services in
Australia, including digital advertising and creator/influencer
advertising services.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers
that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening
of competition. In particular:
a. the parties’ combined share in the supply of digital
advertising services and the supply of creator/influencer
advertising services in Australia is low and the increase in
share of supply arising from the Acquisition would be small
b. there are alternative suppliers of digital advertising services
and creator/influencer advertising services in Australia
c. there appears to be a low risk of foreclosure or other anti-
competitive vertical effects resulting from exclusionary
conduct post-acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
